text:
amy: Quick sync — planning Q next quarter OKRs for DevEx. Need to prioritize SDK surface (python/js/ts), two new quickstarts, and 3 sample apps. customer asks piling up, we should triage.
raj: +1. do we have a list of customer-driven asks to triage?
mira: I pulled the support tickets and SE asks — top asks: better error messages, streaming example, and a native node SDK snippet for websockets.
sam: can we fold streaming + websockets into a single sample app? that'd cover 2 asks.
amy: I like that. propose ranking by impact vs effort. impact = customer count * revenue tier. effort = eng + docs + infra.
raj: rough numbers: streaming sample app ~ 4 dev-weeks, node websocket snippet ~ 1 dev-week, improved errors across SDKs ~ 2 dev-weeks + tests.
jordan: FYI one enterprise customer needs on-prem sample + VPC setup as a template — higher priority if sales wants it.
mira: add that as "on-prem deployment reference" — effort estimate 3w + infra lab.
amy: OK let's agree on launch criteria per initiative. Draft:
```
- SDK improvements (python/js/ts): unit tests, changelog, migration guide, telemetry events, >= 90% code coverage for new modules
- Streaming sample app: end-to-end repo, README quickstart, demo recording, CI deploy to staging, perf baseline (latency & cost)
- Node websocket snippet: runnable snippet, tests, inline playground example in docs
- On-prem reference: infra terraform + README, security checklist, working demo in staging env
```
raj: Add SLO: SDK install + sample quickstart should be <10 minutes to run from repo clone.
amy: Good. Also we need acceptance criteria for "docs parity": at least one tutorial, API reference, and troubleshooting section.
sam: Question: scope for quickstarts — interactive notebook vs runnable app? customers like notebooks for eval, but apps show production flow.
mira: Suggest one of each: notebook for eval (python), and a tiny production sample app (node) that shows streaming + fallback.
jordan: Sales will push for on-prem template — propose we carve a "customer-driven" lane: anything that scores >=8/10 on revenue impact gets expedited and tagged for dedicated resources.
amy: Agreed. Let's capture prioritization matrix columns: impact, effort, revenue signal, strategic alignment, maintenance cost. We can score 1-5.
raj: I'll build the spreadsheet today and add current asks + estimates.
amy: Great. Owners: raj -> prioritization spreadsheet + scoring; mira -> collate support tickets and sample idea drafts; sam -> draft streaming sample app plan and infra needs; jordan -> coordinate sales/customer prioritization; i'll own roadmap finalization and OKR mapping.
alice-bot: Reminder: quarterly planning doc template is available at https://redwood.internal/planning/q-template.
amy: Next steps — raj to share spreadsheet by EOD Friday, we review Monday 10am. If we can get scores by then, we'll lock top 3 initiatives for the quarter.
mira: I'll tag the top customer requests in the spreadsheet and include one-pager per request.
sam: I'll sketch a minimal architecture diagram and list required infra (k8s, tgts, staging GPU) by Sunday.
jordan: I'll surface the revenue-backed asks to the AE team so they can prioritize demos.
amy: Awesome. small ask: keep proposed scope minimal — we can always add stretch goals. :+1:
raj: noted. I'll include a "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" column.
amy: Thanks team. Meeting Monday 10am — calendar invite up.
